provenance.instrument: Lower Saucon Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 180 Zoning, adopted by the Township Council 2-20-2002 by Ord. No. 2002-03, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 LO1675, Township of Lower Saucon (180-15 adopts the 'Zoning Map for the Township of Lower Saucon, Northampton County, PA', and the code cites the Soil Survey of Northampton County). The township website (lowersaucontownship.org, Council, Recently Adopted Ordinances) lists Ord. No. 2026-02 (data centers) and 2026-03 (striking Appendix A from Chapter 180) of 5-20-2026, both in the code, and later ordinances on solid waste (2026-04), stormwater (2026-05) and the official map (2026-06), none of them zoning. The eCode360 New Laws page lists the same three later ordinances. District uses, lot and yard figures are text in each district article. Two attachments are PDFs and were not opened: Appendix B (Accessory Land Uses) and Appendix D (Lot Area and Bulk Chart) Appendix B (Accessory Land Uses, amended through Ord. No. 2019-01) and Appendix D (Lot Area and Bulk Chart, dated 11-01-2008) were read on 2026-11-26. Appendix B has no row for an accessory relative apartment and says the chart is for reference only and not regulation. Appendix D predates later text amendments (for example RA 3 acres and older coverage figures), so the file keeps the district text and 180-127.3A.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 05-20-2026.' New Laws: Ord. No. 2026-04 (Ch 135), 2026-05 (Ch 137) and 2026-06 (official map), none amending Chapter 180
checks: Accessory relative apartments are 'permitted by right within the RA, R80, R40, R20, R12, UR, and VC Zoning Districts' (180-137A). The district accessory use lists (for example 180-45 in R12) do not name them, but 180-137A permits them in those districts

An accessory relative apartment is 'An additional dwelling unit added onto, or created within, a single-family detached dwelling for occupancy by a person or persons related by blood, marriage or adoption to the occupants of the principal dwelling' (180-5B)
Habitable floor area at least 200 sq ft and at most 900 sq ft. No more than two relatives may live in it (180-137A(1))
One apartment per single-family detached dwelling or lot. 'Accessory apartments may not be permitted as a separate structure' (180-137A(2))
The lot area and dimensions of the house and the apartment together must meet the district minimums, and the applicant submits a plan showing it (180-137A(3), (4))

The apartment uses the house's sewer, water and other utilities. No separate systems or connections. On an on-lot septic system or well, the applicant shows the systems can serve everyone, and the Sewage Enforcement Officer reviews any connection or expansion (180-137A(5)). A sewer permit from the Sewage Enforcement Officer is needed for any conversion or expansion of use (180-94A(4))

One more all-weather off-street space for the apartment, on top of the house's own parking (180-137A(6)). A single-family dwelling needs '1 per 0.33 dwelling unit' (180-98C(1)(b)). Under the fraction rule, 'only the fraction shall be counted as one' (180-98C(2)(h)), 1 / 0.33 = 3.03 rounds up to four spaces for the house, so five in total. Read as three for the house, the total is four. No parking in required yards, except that one space for each single-family detached home may be within the front yard setback (180-98C(2)(g))
Except for an exterior stairway, the house may not be altered so that it no longer looks like a single-family detached dwelling (180-137A(7))
Only relatives of the occupants of the house may live in the apartment. Its use ends within three months after no qualified person lives there (180-137A(8))

Outside RA, R80, R40, R20, R12, UR and VC the apartment is not listed. 'No other use shall be permitted unless the Township's elected officials approve an amendment to this chapter' (180-13C). 180-12D lets the Zoning Hearing Board permit a use the chapter does not mention, but the accessory relative apartment is mentioned, so that route is not read as reaching it

Single-family detached dwellings are permitted in RA, R80, R40, R20, R12, MH, UR and VC. GB, LI, LM and O&L list no single-family dwelling (180-67, 180-79, 180-83.2, 180-85). In O&L an existing lot under 50 acres may be used for a single-family residential use (180-89.2)

Conversion: 'The conversion of a single-family detached dwelling to a two-family detached, single-family attached or multifamily dwelling, limited to three dwelling units, provided that the owner resides on the premises' (180-5B). It is a conditional use in R12, UR and VC and permitted by right with site plan approval in GB and LM (180-44A, 180-56B, 180-62B, 180-67A(10), 180-83.2A(8))

Floodplain: 'No structures, filling, piping or regrading shall be permitted within any floodplain' (180-95B(3)(b)), but 180-95B(3)(b)[1] allows a building in a floodplain 'in compliance with Chapter 90'. Chapter 90 prohibits new construction and substantial improvements in any identified floodplain area (90-26, 90-27), and 'No variance shall be granted for any of the prohibited uses or activities in § 90-26' (90-35B). Improvements to an existing structure follow 90-33: none in the floodway (90-33A), no enlargement that would raise the base flood elevation (90-33B), and an improvement under 50% of market value is 'elevated and/or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible' (90-33K). So an addition that is not a substantial improvement may be allowed, and one that is cannot get a variance

Carbonate Geology Areas: no habitable dwelling within 100 ft of the rim of a sinkhole or closed depression, or of ghost lakes, lineaments, fracture traces or disappearing streams, unless a licensed geologist's study and mitigation satisfy the township (180-95B(17)(c)[4])

Natural resources: floodplain soils, wetlands, lakes and ponds may not be built on, and buffers, steep slopes and woodlands have protection rates of 60% to 85% (180-95B). A site plan reviewed by the Zoning Officer is needed for a single-family detached dwelling and its accessory uses (180-95A(4))
Only one building housing a principal use per lot (180-91D)
A nonconforming lot lawful when created and held in separate ownership may be built on if the yards are met (180-99B(2)). 180-137A(3) still asks that the lot meet the district minimum lot area

On-lot sewage: 40,000 sq ft per equivalent dwelling unit with a standard on-lot system (180-94A(1)), and 'A two-acre minimum lot size shall be required per dwelling unit or per equivalent dwelling unit' where the soils need another system (180-94A(2)), and 30,000 sq ft per equivalent dwelling unit with public sewer and an on-lot well (180-94A(3)). The apartment is 'An additional dwelling unit' (180-5B), so on a lot that needs another system the house and the apartment likely need four acres. These figures apply in every district and the most restrictive rule applies, so in R20 and smaller districts they, not the district table, set the lot minimum without public sewer

Impervious cover for single-family detached lots follows the chart in 180-127.3A. A lot of record with a house on it on 3-31-2011 keeps the percentages in effect on that date (180-127.3C), which the online code does not show
Variances: 180-11C sets the usual findings and does not bar a use variance
No accessory building, structure or use may be over a septic tank or a primary or backup drainfield area (180-128D)
In the WP overlay, an on-lot sewage system is inspected by the Sewage Enforcement Officer before an 'expansion or conversion of the land use served' (180-95B(18)(e)[2][d][ii])
In VC a building may have at most 6,000 sq ft of floor area on all floors, the house and the apartment together (180-64E)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Lower Saucon Township Zoning Department. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-16. Read: Article I (180-1 to 180-5, definitions A to N in full and 'Principal building structure or use'), Article II (180-6 to 180-12.2), Article III, every district article (IV to XV, 180-18 to 180-89.2), 180-91 to 180-95 (to 180-95B(18)(e)), 180-98C, 180-99, 180-115, 180-127.3, Article XVIII (180-128 to 180-137), Chapter 90 Article VI (90-24 to 90-31) and the parts of Article VII and 90-35B quoted here, the New Laws page and the township's recently adopted ordinances page. The code search for ADU terms found 180-137 and the 'Conversion' and 'Accessory relative apartment' definitions. Not read: definitions after 'Nontower commercial communications facility' except 'Principal building', 180-95B(18)(f) onward, 180-96, 180-97, 180-98A, B and D onward, 180-100.1 to 180-100.13 (signs), 180-101 to 180-114, 180-116 to 180-127.2, 180-127.4, Chapter 90 Articles I to V and the rest of Articles VII and VIII, Chapter 145, and the PDF attachments (Appendix B Accessory Land Uses, Appendix D Lot Area and Bulk Chart). Second reading 2026-11-26 (G0): Appendices B and D read by cell position (see status_detail); neither lists or limits the accessory relative apartment, and both are reference charts behind the text. Left as disputes the code does not settle: an addition in the Floodplain district as an allowed improvement (90-33) or a barred substantial improvement (90-26, 90-27, 90-35B), shown as disputed; whether 180-94A counts the apartment as a second unit for on-lot sewage (four acres with an alternate system); parking of five (literal fraction rule, 180-98C(2)(h)) or four; and the pre-2011 impervious percentages 180-127.3C keeps for existing lots.

term.note: 'Accessory relative apartment: An additional dwelling unit added onto, or created within, a single-family detached dwelling for occupancy by a person or persons related by blood, marriage or adoption to the occupants of the principal dwelling.'

status.note: 'Accessory relative apartments are permitted by right within the RA, R80, R40, R20, R12, UR, and VC Zoning Districts'. Only relatives of the occupants of the house may live there (180-137A(8))

scope_districts.note: Named in 180-137A. MH, GB, LI, LM and O&L are not named

status_outside.note: 'Every building or other structure may be erected or used and each parcel of land may be used or occupied only for the uses permitted by right and the uses permitted by conditional use and special exception in the zoning district in which the building or lot is located unless otherwise allowed by this chapter. No other use shall be permitted unless the Township's elected officials approve an amendment to this chapter.' 180-137A names seven districts only

status_by_form.note: 'Accessory apartments may not be permitted as a separate structure.' A unit in a detached garage or other accessory building is a separate structure

path.note: Permitted by right with a zoning permit. The applicant submits a plan showing the district's dimensional requirements are met (180-137A(4))

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board. The usual findings. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Conversion to up to three units, owner on the premises (R12, UR, VC)
value.conditions: 'Conversion' of a single-family detached dwelling to a two-family detached, single-family attached or multifamily dwelling, 'limited to three dwelling units, provided that the owner resides on the premises' (180-5B). A conditional use before the Township Council with site plan approval (180-44A, 180-56B, 180-62B). 'The lot area per dwelling unit shall not be reduced to less than the amount stated for the district', each unit meets the district yard, impervious and parking rules, no exterior structural change except for health and safety, and at least 450 sq ft of floor area per unit (180-115). Parking 'Conversion: 1 per 0.5 dwelling unit' (180-98C)

requires.condition: An existing single-family detached dwelling is converted
The owner lives on the premises

value.note: The lot figures read the district minimum lot area (R12 12,000, UR 8,000, VC 8,000 sq ft) as the lot area per dwelling unit, for two units. VC also allows 'Only one principal use' per lot and a building of at most 6,000 sq ft of floor area (180-64)

value.name: Conversion to up to three units, owner on the premises (GB, LM)
value.conditions: Conversion is a permitted use with site plan approval in GB and LM (180-67A(10)(b), 180-83.2A(8)(b)). Same standards as above (180-115). Neither district lists a single-family detached dwelling, so this reaches an existing house

requires.condition: An existing single-family detached dwelling is converted
The owner lives on the premises

value.note: The lot figure reads the 40,000 sq ft district minimum (180-70A, 180-83.5A) as the lot area per dwelling unit, for two units

building_types.note: 'added onto, or created within, a single-family detached dwelling' and 'within a single-family detached dwelling or on a single-family detached lot'

requires_conforming_lot.note: 'The lot area and dimensions of the principal dwelling and the accessory apartment combined must meet the minimum lot area and dimensional requirements for the applicable zoning district.' Read as the district minimum for the lot, not twice it. A nonconforming lot of record may otherwise be built on if the yards are met (180-99B(2))

value.condition: Only a single-family detached dwelling qualifies. A twin ('single-family semidetached', each unit on its own lot) or a townhouse ('single-family attached') does not.

The apartment must connect to the house's sewer, water and other utilities, with no separate systems or connections. On an on-lot septic system or well, the applicant shows the systems can serve everyone in both units, or gets approval to expand them, and the Sewage Enforcement Officer reviews the connection.
Except for an exterior stairway, the house may not be altered in a way that departs from its look as a single-family detached dwelling.
The apartment may be used only while a relative of the occupants of the house lives there, and must stop being used within three months after no qualified person lives there.

In the Floodplain district, a building is allowed only in compliance with Chapter 90. Chapter 90 prohibits new construction and any substantial improvement in an identified floodplain area, and no variance may be granted for them.

disputed_by.note: Chapter 90 Article VII lets an existing structure be improved. 'No expansion or enlargement of an existing structure shall be allowed within any identified floodplain area that would cause any increase in BFE' (90-33B), none in the floodway (90-33A), and an improvement under 50% of market value is 'elevated and/or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible' (90-33K). So an addition that is not a substantial improvement may be allowed

value.condition: In the Floodplain district, work inside the house that is a substantial improvement is prohibited by Chapter 90, and no variance may be granted for it. A smaller improvement is elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible, and none is allowed in the floodway. A habitable building's adjacent ground must be at least 1.5 ft above the 100-year flood level.

In a Carbonate Geology Area (and within 500 ft of one), no habitable dwelling may be within 100 ft of the rim of a sinkhole or closed depression, or of ghost lakes, lineaments, fracture traces or disappearing streams, unless a licensed geologist's investigation and mitigation satisfy the township.

Without public sewer, 180-94A sets 40,000 sq ft per equivalent dwelling unit for a standard on-lot system, and 'A two-acre minimum lot size shall be required per dwelling unit or per equivalent dwelling unit' where the soils need another system. With public sewer and an on-lot well it sets 30,000 sq ft per equivalent dwelling unit. The apartment is 'An additional dwelling unit', so on a lot that needs another system the house and the apartment likely need four acres. Whether the standard system figure counts the apartment is not settled.
The addition may not be built over a septic tank or a primary or backup drainfield area.
In the WP overlay, the Sewage Enforcement Officer inspects an on-lot sewage system before an expansion or conversion of the land use it serves.
In VC a building may have at most 6,000 sq ft of floor area on all floors. The house and the apartment together count.

Impervious cover on a single-family detached lot follows the chart in 180-127.3A. A lot that was lawful, of record and held a principal structure on 3-31-2011 is not held to the on-lot chart and keeps the percentages in effect on that date, which the online code does not show.

types_allowed.note: 'added onto, or created within, a single-family detached dwelling'. 'Accessory apartments may not be permitted as a separate structure'

max_sqft.note: 'The habitable floor area of the accessory apartment shall be no less than 200 square feet and no greater than 900 square feet.'

internal_uses_district_height.note: The apartment is part of the house, so the district height applies

occupancy.value: At most two people, who must be related by blood, marriage or adoption to the people living in the house. Its use ends within three months after no relative lives there.

owner_occupancy.note: No owner rule. The occupants must be related to the occupants of the principal dwelling

max_adus.note: 'Only one accessory apartment may be permitted within a single-family detached dwelling or on a single-family detached lot.'

spaces_required.note: 'A minimum of one all-weather off-street parking space, with unrestricted ingress and egress to the street, shall be provided for the accessory apartment, in addition to that required for the principal dwelling.'

reading.value: Five in all on the literal rule: the table asks '1 per 0.33 dwelling unit' for a single-family dwelling, 3.03 spaces, and a fraction counts as one, so four for the house and one more for the apartment. Read as three for the house, the total is four. No parking in required yards, except one space for a single-family detached home may be in the front yard setback (180-98C(2)(g)).

total_on_site.note: '1 per 0.33 dwelling unit' for the house is 3.03 spaces, and 'only the fraction shall be counted as one', so four for the house and one for the apartment

max_impervious_coverage.note: The chart lists RA with 'Maximum Site Impervious Coverage' 20% and says individual on-lot values 'are a function of the design/layout of the site'

value.when: Standard on-lot sewage disposal (trench, seepage bed or sand filter)
value.note: The RA district minimum is larger than 40,000 sq ft and holds. 'area shall be 40,000 square feet per equivalent dwelling unit'. Where the soils need another on-lot system, 'A two-acre minimum lot size shall be required per dwelling unit' (180-94A(2)), so the house and the apartment likely need four acres

value.when: Public sewer with an on-lot well
value.note: 'area shall be 30,000 square feet per equivalent dwelling unit'
